newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 closes higher despite blue chip losses.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 closes higher despite blue chip losses.

text.p: The Czech PX50 index rose again on Tuesday despite further losses to blue chips which analysts said was part of a region-wide trend towards profit taking. The PX50 rose 0.2 percent to 629 while the high cap dominated RPIX fell 0.02 percent to 1,352.5.
"I think we've seen profit taking across the whole region. We've seen Hungary and Poland leading and the Czech Republic following," said John Vax, director of capital markets at ING Barings.
"We still continue to see more interest in selling blue chips right now than buying," added Vax.
The blue chip decline was led again by Komercni Banka with the PX50 index's two most heavily capitalised shares SPT Telecom and CEZ also moving lower.
Among the bourse's gainers, tobacco company Tabak, 77 percent owned by Philip Morris, continued its run of spectacular gains to post another year of 8,550.
Petrochemical stocks also showed now sign of slowing down. Chemopetrol rose 47 crowns to 1,494 and Kaucuk rose 75 crowns to 1,578.
